title: Redact secrets in config diffs before rendering to Slack
author: Devon Price
description: Problem: Incident-bot v2 is starting to surface tenant-safe config diffs in #incidents and #eng-oncall, but the current formatting is purely syntactic and can leak secrets if upstream config contains inline credentials/tokens (or if a value looks like a secret). This PR adds a deterministic redaction layer that runs before any diff content is rendered to Slack (cards, modals, and copy-to-clipboard). Approach: (1) Add key-based redaction (denylist of sensitive key names + path-based matches). (2) Add value-based secret detection (JWTs, API keys, common token prefixes, PEM blocks, base64-ish long strings, AWS-like access keys, etc.) with conservative thresholds. (3) Add allowlisted keys/paths that are safe to show even if they trip generic heuristics (e.g., numeric limits, routing weights, non-sensitive feature flag booleans). (4) Replace redacted values with stable placeholders ("[REDACTED:key]" / "[REDACTED:pattern]"), preserving diff structure for incident triage. (5) Add tests ensuring we never render raw secret patterns to Slack output (unit tests + golden snapshots for Slack blocks). Also adds a visible warning banner when redaction occurs and a counter metric to help tune false positives over time. Notes: This PR does not change authorization; it is a defense-in-depth layer. It intentionally over-redacts in ambiguous cases. Follow-up: align patterns with redwood/config-service redaction hooks once that endpoint ships (ENG-5422) and wire audit events for "redaction_applied" vs "no_redaction" for easier compliance review.
commits: Add redaction pipeline for config diffs (key + value heuristics)
Introduce allowlist + path matcher for known-safe fields
Add secret pattern detectors (JWT/PEM/token prefixes) + thresholds
Slack rendering: show redaction warning + preserve diff formatting
Tests: snapshot Slack blocks + fuzz-ish cases for secret patterns
conversation: Miles Thornton (review): Can we guarantee that *all* Slack surfaces (thread card + modal + any “expand” action) go through the same redaction path? I don’t want a path where the card is safe but the modal leaks. Devon Price (author): Yep — pushed the formatter down so both blocks + modal call formatConfigDiff(), which always redacts. Added a test that renders both block types and asserts the raw secret strings are absent. Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): The allowlist makes me nervous. Are we allowlisting by exact key only, or by path? Also please avoid allowlisting anything that could be tenant-provided strings (names, descriptions) because those can contain accidental secrets. Devon Price: It’s path-aware (JSON pointer-ish) and limited to numeric/bool fields we already rely on for incident debugging (routing weights, quota limits, feature flags booleans). I removed “description” and “notes” from the early draft allowlist. Marcus Lin (review): Pattern detector: add PEM block coverage and be careful with base64 detection — false positives are likely on hashed IDs. Suggest thresholding on length + entropy-ish heuristic. Devon Price: Added PEM begin/end matcher + updated base64 rule: requires (a) >= 32 chars, (b) high alphabet ratio, and (c) not purely hex. Also added explicit bypass for UUID-like values. Benji Okafor (review): We should preserve diff readability. Are we redacting the entire line or only the value? Devon Price: Only the value. Keys + structural diff markers remain so you can still see *what changed*. Also added a count of redacted fields and a banner in Slack: “Some values redacted (N)”. Miles Thornton: LGTM once CI is green. (later) CI passed. Approved.
checks: CI (incident-bot): lint ✅, typecheck ✅, unit tests ✅, Slack snapshot tests ✅; Security hooks: secret-scan ✅ (no new secrets detected); Build: docker image ✅
release_notes: Incident-bot: Config diff output now redacts secret-like values and sensitive keys before rendering in Slack; adds redaction warning banner and metrics for tuning false positives.
